body.statement: At \(P_0\in\mathcal M_I\), simultaneous oracle adaptation holds if and only if the observable simultaneous Gram discrepancy in \(\mathrm{def{:}oracle\text{-}gram\text{-}tests}\) is zero; equivalently, \(V_U=V_{\mathrm{PT}}=V_{\mathrm{SC}}\) if and only if \(\phi_{\mathrm{PT}}=\phi_{\mathrm{SC}}\) in \(L^2(P_{0,O})\). One-sided PT adaptation \(V_U=V_{\mathrm{PT}}\) holds if and only if the PT-oracle Gram discrepancy is zero, and one-sided SC adaptation \(V_U=V_{\mathrm{SC}}\) holds if and only if the SC-oracle Gram discrepancy is zero. These are finite covariance-matrix tests in \(\Omega_x\), \(a_x^{\mathrm{or}}\), and \(d_x^{\mathrm{or}}\), all identified from the observed law.
body.justification: Necessary-and-sufficient criteria distinguish genuine oracle adaptation from accidental equality of reported standard errors.
body.gap: TchetgenTchetgenRobinsRotnitzky2010 establishes local efficiency at one intersection model, whereas no cited result gives simultaneous and one-sided iff adaptation criteria for two nonnested ATT branches with different restriction derivatives.
body.consumer: An applied analyst can diagnose from estimated derivative constraints whether identification robustness is asymptotically free in a particular short-panel design.
body.proof_tex:
Use the notation \(\psi_{\mathrm{PT},x}(a)\) and \(\psi_{\mathrm{SC},x}(d)\) from the proof of \(\mathrm{thm{:}union\text{-}envelope}\).  By the tangent normal form and the definition of the oracle coefficients,
\[
 \phi_{\mathrm{PT}}=\sum_x\psi_{\mathrm{PT},x}(a_x^{\mathrm{or}}),
 \qquad
 \phi_{\mathrm{SC}}=\sum_x\psi_{\mathrm{SC},x}(d_x^{\mathrm{or}}).
 \tag{1}
\]
Disjoint stratum support and \(p_X(x)>0\) imply
\[
 \|\phi_{\mathrm{PT}}-\phi_{\mathrm{SC}}\|_{P_0}^2
 =\sum_xp_X(x)c(a_x^{\mathrm{or}},d_x^{\mathrm{or}})'
   \Omega_xc(a_x^{\mathrm{or}},d_x^{\mathrm{or}}).
 \tag{2}
\]
The right side is the simultaneous Gram discrepancy.  It is nonnegative and is zero exactly when the two canonical gradients are equal in \(L^2(P_{0,O})\).

Let \(A=\mathcal I_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_0)\), \(B=\mathcal I_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0)\), and \(C=A\cap B\).  These are closed affine subsets of a Hilbert space: their direction spaces are finite spans of restriction normals.  The union theorem proves \(C\ne\varnothing\), and \(C\subseteq A\).  Since the squared norm is strictly convex as a function of the represented Hilbert-space element, its minimizer on \(A\) is unique.  It follows that
\[
 V_U=V_{\mathrm{PT}}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \phi_{\mathrm{PT}}\in C
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \phi_{\mathrm{PT}}\in B.
 \tag{3}
\]
The final condition in (3), using (1) and the normal form for \(B\), is equivalent to the existence of \((d_x)_x\) for which
\[
 \sum_xp_X(x)c(a_x^{\mathrm{or}},d_x)'\Omega_xc(a_x^{\mathrm{or}},d_x)=0.
\]
The finite-dimensional minimum is attained, including in singular designs after redundant rows are removed, so this is exactly zero PT-oracle discrepancy.  Interchanging PT and SC proves
\[
 V_U=V_{\mathrm{SC}}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \min_{(a_x)}\sum_xp_X(x)c(a_x,d_x^{\mathrm{or}})'\Omega_xc(a_x,d_x^{\mathrm{or}})=0.
 \tag{4}
\]
Finally, simultaneous equality implies by (3)--(4) that both branch canonical gradients equal the unique minimum-norm element of \(C\), and hence equal each other.  Conversely, if \(\phi_{\mathrm{PT}}=\phi_{\mathrm{SC}}\), that common function belongs to \(C\) and is no larger in norm than any member of \(C\), so all three bounds coincide.  Equation (2) proves the equivalent simultaneous Gram test.  Every entry of the displayed programs is a conditional second moment of the observed-data vector \(h_x\), so the tests are observed-law functionals.
